content.value: Rideable animals have different jobs instead of being weaker versions of one another. Horses remain the premium overworld speed mount; donkeys specialize in cargo; mules combine horse mobility with donkey logistics; camels support long two-player expeditions; striders dominate lava travel; skeleton horses are durable unusual mounts; and pigs are inexpensive early couriers.
Equipping a Chest

Use a normal Chest on an adult mount to attach it. The chest is consumed outside Creative mode, appears on the animal, and unlocks that mount's cargo slots. Horse-family mounts also show a dedicated chest slot in their normal inventory. Camels, pigs, and striders open their shared cargo screen with the inventory key while riding, or by sneak-using them with an empty hand; while riding a chest-equipped pig, using an empty hand on the pig opens its cargo directly. Large donkey and mule inventories stay inside the vanilla panel and can be scrolled with the mouse wheel or scrollbar.

Pig: 3 cargo slots.
Horse: 6 cargo slots.
Skeleton Horse: 6 cargo slots.
Strider: 6 cargo slots.
Camel: 12 cargo slots.
Mule: 15-24 genetically determined slots.
Donkey: 15-33 genetically determined slots.

A chest can only be removed from its equipment slot while every cargo slot is empty. If the mount dies, its chest and cargo drop into the world. Shulker boxes, barrels, storage upgrades, and cargo weight do not change these limits.
Only the owner can change the chest on an owned horse-family mount. Pigs and striders have no vanilla owner, so their storage is public. Saddle, body armour, and chest equipment are independent.
Donkeys: Pack Logistics

Donkeys inherit Health, Travel Speed, Endurance, Trail Skill, and Pack Capacity. Wild Pack Capacity begins between 15 and 21 and breeding can raise it to 33. Packmaster adds two usable slots without exceeding 33. Hold Sprint while moving to use Pack Trot: it grants 10-15% speed according to Trail Skill and normally spends 2 Endurance per second. Recognized road and common building surfaces add another 5-15% speed according to Trail Skill.

Packmaster: +2 cargo slots, up to 33.
Tireless: 15% more Endurance and reduced Pack Trot cost.
Sure-Footed: improved step height, safe falling, and knockback resistance.
Sturdy: +15 armour.
Mules: Expedition Hybrids

A Mule is the sterile result of breeding an eligible Horse with an eligible Donkey of the opposite sex. It combines Health, Speed, and Jump from the horse line with Endurance and Pack Capacity from the donkey line. Mule cargo is about 75% of its donkey parent's capacity, clamped to 15-24 slots to preserve the vanilla horse-inventory layout. Mules use a faster Pack Trot than donkeys but can never produce offspring.
Camels: Two-Rider Expeditions

Camels inherit Health, Cruise Speed, Dash Power, Endurance, and Dash Efficiency. Dash Power scales the distance of the vanilla camel dash; Dash Efficiency reduces its Endurance cost. They carry 12 slots and retain their defining ability to transport two riders.
Striders: Lava Travel

Striders inherit Health, Lava Speed, Heat Capacity, Heat Retention, and Stability. Their Heat resource recovers rapidly in lava and drains slowly while cold outside it; Heat Retention reduces that cold loss. Hold Sprint and Forward in lava to activate Lava Rush. Stability improves its bonus and Heatkeeper reduces its cost. Striders receive four breeding attempts and a 20-minute cooldown.
Skeleton Horses: Soul Bond

Skeleton Horses do not breed and have fixed starting genes. Riding raises Soul Bond by one for every 10 travelled blocks, up to 100. At Bond 10, open the inventory and make one permanent specialization choice using the three vanilla-style buttons.

Tidebound: strong water movement efficiency and Water Breathing for its controlling rider, turning the skeleton horse into an aquatic mount.
Graveguard: 20% more base maximum health and +20 armour for dangerous expeditions.
Stormrunner: 15% more base movement speed and 40% lightning resistance.
A skeleton-horse specialization cannot be changed after selection. The short Tide, Guard, and Storm button labels correspond to Tidebound, Graveguard, and Stormrunner.
Training & Breeding

Donkeys, mules, camels, striders, skeleton horses, and pigs train from controlled travel using the same early-friendly level curve as horses. Every accumulated 10 horizontal blocks awards 2 XP, or 4 while the mount's active travel ability is running. Levels add health and a small amount of movement speed.

Donkeys, camels, and striders use persistent male or female genetics. A breeding pair must be opposite-sex, have attempts remaining, be off cooldown, and not be directly or ancestrally related. Each child selects the better parent for at least three genes, normally has a 70% better-value chance per gene, receives a small lineage gain, and can mutate. Donkeys and camels have three attempts and a 30-minute cooldown; striders have four attempts and a 20-minute cooldown.

Road recognition is data-driven through the cranks-dungeons:horse_roads block tag. Dirt paths, gravel, stone and brick families, planks, slabs, stairs, and many common construction blocks work by default, including the normal block palettes used by configurable road-generation mods.

Mounted hearts for every supported mount use the mod's scale of 5 health per full heart. All genetic, training, trait, cargo, and travel bonuses belong exclusively to the animal; riders do not receive those attributes.
